content.title: Which Need of Yours Can Allah Not Fulfill?
content.subtitle: To the Lord who parted the sea to make a path, your request is effortless!
content.body:
When you lay your head on the pillow in the stillness of the night and the day's noise fades away, the unfulfilled desires buried in your heart rise to the surface, don't they?

Some carry a mountain of debt, others face family turmoil; some are searching desperately for halal sustenance, while others wait years hoping to see the face of a child. Over time, we grow tired of making dua. Subtly, a doubt creeps into our hearts: "Will Allah truly grant me this? Will my impossible wish ever come true?"

Are We Considering People More Powerful Than Our Lord?

This modern, materialistic world has quietly planted a lie in our minds. We have begun believing that a boss’s favor, an official's recommendation, or a hefty bank balance is what truly changes our destiny.

Yet, we doubt the power of the very Lord who put ink in that boss’s pen and controls that official's heartbeat! Even if every door on earth slams shut, the doors of the heavens never close.

The Parable of the Ocean and a Needle

No matter how massive your need is, could it ever be greater than Allah’s treasures?

In Sahih Muslim (2577), Allah says in a Hadith Qudsi: "O My servants, were the first and the last of you, human and jinn, to stand in one plain and ask of Me, and were I to give everyone what they asked for, that would not decrease what I have any more than a needle decreases the sea if dipped into it."

Think about it! The Being who blessed Zakariya (AS) with a child in old age (Surah Maryam: 3-9), brought Isa (AS) into the world without a father (Surah Maryam: 19-21), turned Namrud’s blazing fire into a cool garden for Ibrahim (AS) (Surah Al-Anbiya: 69), and split the raging sea into twelve dry paths for Musa (AS) (Surah Ash-Shu'ara: 63)—that very Lord is still upon the Mighty Throne. Has His power diminished by even an atom? Never!

Why You Must Never Give Up on Dua

Often, we pray for a few days and grow impatient. In Sahih al-Bukhari (6340), the Prophet ﷺ warned that a servant’s dua is answered so long as they do not grow hasty and say, "I prayed, but I was not answered."

A sincere dua never goes in vain. Either Allah grants what you asked for, averts a calamity in its place, or stores a reward for the Hereafter so vast that on Judgment Day you will wish, "If only none of my duas had been answered in the world!" (Musnad Ahmad: 11133). This certainty keeps a believer steady like a mountain in life's fiercest storms.

The One Who Sees Your Wounds Will Heal Them

Perhaps you carry a deep wound whose pain nobody understands. People see your smile, while only your Lord sees the silent tears soaking your pillow at night. Remember, Allah does not test you just to cause pain; He calls you to His court to mend your broken heart into something more beautiful.

Hold onto His promise: "Indeed, with hardship comes ease." (Surah Ash-Sharh: 6). Your long wait will never go to waste. Cast aside all grievances, fall into prostration, and whisper to the Owner of the Throne:

"O Allah! No human holds any power, and none has the cure for my wounds. You alone can remove my troubles and scarcity, and erase every unbearable pain. Grant peace to my heart."

Have faith—the Lord who revives dead land with rain will surely breathe new life into your weary heart.
